Linux Mint Cinnamon.label: Familiar everyday computing
Linux Mint Cinnamon.description: A traditional interface with an application menu and established tools. Cinnamon helps you get started and handle everyday tasks.

Zorin OS Core.label: An easier transition
Zorin OS Core.description: A tidy interface with familiar controls helps people switching from Windows. Its Ubuntu foundation provides a wide choice of software.

Ubuntu.label: Versatile and well documented
Ubuntu.description: A large community and a wide choice of software. The GNOME interface brings applications and windows together in a central overview.

Kubuntu.label: Ubuntu with plenty of settings
Kubuntu.description: An Ubuntu foundation with KDE Plasma: traditional desktop controls and many options for adjusting appearance and behavior.

Debian.label: Consistency comes first
Debian.description: Thoroughly tested software and long-term maintenance take priority. Applications are often less recent than in distributions that introduce changes more frequently.

Fedora Workstation.label: Recent software with GNOME
Fedora Workstation.description: Modern software and a tidy GNOME interface. New major releases arrive frequently and require regular release upgrades.

Fedora KDE Plasma Desktop.label: Recent and customizable
Fedora KDE Plasma Desktop.description: Fedora combines modern software with KDE Plasma. Many settings let you adjust appearance and behavior; regular release upgrades are part of its maintenance.

openSUSE Leap.label: A consistent desktop foundation
openSUSE Leap.description: Stability-focused releases and system administration tools. With an appropriate setup, you can restore earlier system states.

openSUSE Tumbleweed.label: Rolling updates with a way back
openSUSE Tumbleweed.description: New software arrives through rolling updates that undergo automated testing. A typical setup saves system states to help you undo changes.

MX Linux Xfce.label: Practical and resource-efficient
MX Linux Xfce.description: A Debian foundation with the resource-efficient Xfce interface. MX tools help you set up and manage the system.

Linux Lite.label: An approachable start with Xfce
Linux Lite.description: An Ubuntu foundation with a resource-efficient, traditional Xfce interface. Its own tools help you get started and set up the system.

elementary OS.label: Consistent and tidy
elementary OS.description: A deliberately simple interface with applications designed to work together. Customization is more limited than on many other desktops.

Pop!_OS COSMIC.label: Organize your windows with COSMIC
Pop!_OS COSMIC.description: The COSMIC interface offers many settings and can automatically arrange windows side by side. Its focus is on productive work.

Bazzite.label: Built around gaming
Bazzite.description: A Fedora-based system with preconfigured gaming tools and a focus on Steam. Updates replace the system foundation together, with earlier system states available to select again.

Nobara.label: Gaming and media creation
Nobara.description: A Fedora variant adapted for gaming and multimedia. Additional tools help you get started; setup and maintenance follow the Nobara project’s guidance.

CachyOS.label: Arch with a performance focus
CachyOS.description: An Arch-based distribution with performance tuning and continuously updated software. Preconfigured tools help you get started; regular system maintenance is still required.

EndeavourOS.label: Arch with a head start
EndeavourOS.description: Close to Arch Linux, with installation assistance and a preconfigured interface. Software is continuously updated; setup and maintenance require a hands-on approach.

Arch Linux.label: Assemble your own Linux system
Arch Linux.description: A minimal foundation for building your own system. Installation, interface selection and ongoing maintenance are largely up to you.

NixOS.label: Your system as a blueprint
NixOS.description: You describe the setup in configuration files and can apply it again. Earlier system states remain available to select; the distinctive approach takes time to learn.

Omarchy.label: Arrange windows automatically
Omarchy.description: A preconfigured Arch environment that automatically arranges windows side by side and emphasizes keyboard controls. Its unfamiliar working style takes time to learn.

Solus.label: Independent and desktop-focused
Solus.description: An independent distribution with preconfigured desktop interfaces and its own software selection. Rolling updates keep the system current.

Gentoo Linux.label: Shape Linux in detail
Gentoo Linux.description: Software features and the system layout can be tailored closely to your needs. Programs can be built from source or installed as ready-made packages; setup and maintenance take time and experience.

TUXEDO OS.label: KDE with TUXEDO tools
TUXEDO OS.description: A preconfigured KDE Plasma interface with additional tools from TUXEDO Computers. A key focus is integration with supported devices from this manufacturer.

Void Linux.label: A lean foundation to make your own
Void Linux.description: An independent distribution with rolling updates and a lean system layout. Software selection, setup and maintenance require a hands-on approach and experience.

antiX.label: Lightweight on older computers
antiX.description: A Debian-based distribution with a particularly resource-efficient interface for older or less powerful computers. It offers versatile tools for running directly from a USB drive.
